summary: Suggestions beta: Risk level label is confusing to non-technical stakeholders (needs clearer explanation + shareable language)
description:
Issue summary:
Arkadia Finance (Optimize Suggestions beta) reports that the “Risk: Low/Medium/High” label in the Console Suggestions view is being interpreted by internal stakeholders as security/compliance risk (or “chance Redwood is wrong”), rather than “likelihood of latency/reliability regression if you apply the recommended batching/caching change.” They requested clearer, shareable language for governance review and change-management tickets.

Impact:
- Slows adoption of Suggestions recommendations (internal approvals blocked)
- Increases back-and-forth with platform governance/security teams
- Risk of miscommunication: stakeholders assume “High risk” implies security risk

Where this shows up:
- Suggestions list table risk badge tooltip
- Details drawer “Risk” section copy
- Beta docs page (glossary / definitions)

Customer request:
1) Rename/clarify what “risk” means (performance/reliability risk, not security)
2) Add a short explanation that can be pasted into an internal change request
3) Provide guidance on how to safely validate a suggestion (rollout controls, canary, monitor p95)

Customer context:
- Using Suggestions for batching/caching recommendations on 2 high-traffic routes
- Stakeholder group includes platform governance and security reviewers

Notes:
This is not a product defect; it’s primarily UX/copy + docs clarity. Customer asked for near-term mitigation while we consider longer-term labeling changes (e.g., “Performance risk”).
comments: 2026-02-22 09:18 (Dev Patel, Support) — Ticket created from CS escalation. Customer quote: “Our security review board flagged ‘High risk’ as a compliance concern. We need wording that clearly states this is performance risk only, and what we should monitor.”

2026-02-22 11:02 (Miguel Santos, Customer Success) — Confirmed on call with Arkadia: They’re screenshotting the Suggestions page into internal approval docs. They want a one-liner definition + a second line with concrete guardrails (e.g., canary rollout, watch p95 + error rate). Asked if we can add a doc link directly in the tooltip/drawer.

2026-02-22 12:10 (Marissa Cole, Product - Console) — Agree this is a priority for beta trust. Proposed copy direction: explicitly say “Performance & reliability risk” and add a tooltip line: “Not a security/compliance risk.” Also add “How we calculate risk” deep-link to docs. Looping in Design + Docs.

2026-02-23 10:41 (Kenji Nakamura, Design) — Reviewed current tooltip. It only says “Likelihood of negative impact” which is too vague. Suggest: 1) Rename section header in drawer to “Performance risk” (if feasible without re-layout), 2) Tooltip: “Estimates likelihood of latency or error-rate regression when applying this config change. Not a security risk.” 3) Add examples in the drawer: “Why this is Medium: traffic is bursty; batching could increase p95.”

2026-02-23 14:06 (Sana Farid, Risk/Confidence DS) — +1. Also recommend we avoid implying quality risk since beta scope is batching/caching. We can mention “reliability (timeouts/queueing)” and “latency (p95)” but not “model output quality.” If we mention quality at all, it should be phrased as “No expected output-quality change for batching/caching; monitor as usual.”

2026-02-24 09:32 (Elliot Price, Docs) — Drafted docs additions: a short glossary entry and a ‘How to roll out safely’ section with concrete steps (canary, compare baseline, watch p95/p99 + 5xx/429 + timeouts). Will also add a note: “Risk labels are conservative and based on observed traffic patterns; not guarantees.”

2026-02-25 16:20 (Nora Ahmed, Console UX Eng) — Implemented copy updates behind the existing Suggestions beta flag. Proposed UI changes: 
- Tooltip title: “Performance & reliability risk”
- Tooltip body: “How likely applying this suggestion is to increase latency or error rate for this route. Not a security/compliance risk.”
- Drawer: added “What to monitor” bullets (p95 latency, timeouts/5xx, queue depth if available).
Pending PM/Design final approval.

2026-02-26 10:05 (Miguel Santos, Customer Success) — Shared the updated wording with Arkadia for review (screenshot + text). Customer responded that this resolves their governance confusion and asked for the docs link they can reference in change tickets.

2026-02-27 13:48 (Dev Patel, Support) — Closing loop: Doc updates merged and Console copy queued for next beta patch rollout. Provided customer with a pasteable definition + rollout checklist (see Resolution).
resolution_notes:
Resolution:
1) Console UX copy/tooltip update (beta):
- Clarified that “Risk” refers to performance & reliability risk (latency/error-rate regression likelihood) when applying the suggested batching/caching change.
- Explicitly stated: “Not a security/compliance risk.”
- Added “What to monitor” guidance in the details drawer.

2) Documentation update:
- Added a “Risk level” definition section and a short rollout checklist (canary + monitor p95 latency, 5xx/timeouts, and traffic changes).
- Added language that estimates and risk labels are conservative and not guarantees.

Customer-facing mitigation shared:
Pasteable language for Arkadia’s internal change request:
“Risk level indicates the likelihood that enabling this batching/caching configuration will negatively impact performance (e.g., p95 latency) or reliability (e.g., timeouts/5xx) for the selected route based on observed traffic patterns. It does not represent security or compliance risk. Apply via a canary rollout and monitor p95 latency, timeouts/5xx, and request volume during the change window.”

Follow-ups / references:
- Copy guidelines tracked in risk-level definition spec and the Suggestions beta docs page.
- If we continue to see confusion, PM will consider renaming the label globally to “Performance risk” (requires design sign-off and potential table column rename).
next_steps: Monitor additional beta feedback for ongoing confusion about “risk” semantics; if repeated, evaluate renaming the column header to “Performance risk” in the list view.
Add the docs deep-link in the UI where feasible without clutter (tooltip/footer link), subject to design review.
Ensure Support macros include the pasteable definition above for future tickets.
